chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not create anything in the sky without having an equivalent of it on earth, and He did not create anything on earth without having an equivalent of it in the sky. So when a righteous man from the people of the earth dies, an equivalent of him from the people of the sky ascends, and when a wicked man from the people of the sky dies, an equivalent of him from the people of the earth descends.

key_terms.أَهْلِ السَّمَاءِ: the people of the sky (angels/spiritual beings)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between righteous people on earth and entities in the sky according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to illustrate the Shia concept of *al-Azwaj al-Samawiyya* (heavenly counterparts), emphasizing the ontological link between the terrestrial and celestial realms. This cosmic mirroring underscores the spiritual significance of individual actions, where the fate of the righteous and wicked on earth is reflected by corresponding movements of angels or jinn in the heavens, reinforcing the interconnectedness of the visible and invisible worlds.
